task: Compare parameter WRITE effects through a forwarding ordinary function.
observation: For relay(values) calling push_one(values), C++ reported WRITE while Java reported READ even though push_one mutates the vector parameter.
impact: Java's function access-mode fixed point now propagates WRITE through ordinary helper arguments and handles declaration order independently. The focused effects query matches C++.

resolution.summary: Direct helper WRITE forwarding matches C++ and has a reverse-declaration-order test; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Imported helper and nested field WRITE closure remain open.

task: Compare function parameter WRITE effects for a nested object method receiver path.
observation: For relay(box) calling box.sink.bump(), C++ reported box: WRITE while Java reported READ because the Java parameter effect scan only looked for a direct method on box.
impact: Java function parameter inference now resolves the nested receiver field path and uses the called method's checked receiver WRITE mode. The focused effects query matches C++.

resolution.summary: Nested receiver WRITE mode propagates to the root function parameter and matches C++ query output; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Aliases and generic/cross-module fields remain open.

task: Check CONSUME propagation for generic functions with inferred parameter types.
observation: For take(value) returning value and relay(value) forwarding through take, C++ rejected reuse of a concrete owned Payload while Java accepted it because summary inference ignored checked parameter TypeRefs when no annotation was present.
impact: Java function access summary inference now uses the retained checked parameter TypeRef as a fallback. The generic owned-value reproducer now rejects caller reuse while the Int identity control remains accepted.

resolution.summary: Generic inferred parameter ownership matches C++ for a concrete owned argument, with an Int non-consumption control; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Generic cross-module summaries remain open.

task: Compare function parameter WRITE effects when forwarding an argument to a mutating object method.
observation: For relay(values, box) calling box.append_to(values), C++ reported values: WRITE while Java reported READ because function mutation summaries did not inspect method parameter access modes.
impact: Java function access inference now resolves the method receiver and checks method argument WRITE modes, propagating WRITE to the forwarded function parameter. The focused C++/Java effects queries agree.

resolution.summary: Method argument WRITE propagates through function parameter summaries and matches C++ query output; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Generic and imported method arguments remain open.
